title: Preservation and progress of determinant elimination
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, let $D_0\in\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$, and let $s$ be a determinant-elimination state satisfying the invariant that its row list has the stated matrix dimensions, all entries and the determinant accumulator lie in the range from $0$ to $p-1$, the row counter is at most the dimension, every row in the final $\text{row counter}$ positions has first entry zero, and the determinant of the represented matrix times the accumulator equals $D_0$. Then the state obtained by one determinant-elimination step still satisfies this invariant. If the measure of $s$ is positive, the measure strictly decreases after the step; if its measure is zero, the step leaves $s$ unchanged.
caveat: The invariant is a conjunction of precise conditions on the row array, counters, and determinant; the concise description summarizes rather than expands all indexed clauses.
